sources.title: INAH, Cempoala archaeological site
sources.note: Original institutional indexed page: multiethnic center, tribute, 1519 alliance, wastewater and buildings. Its opening 900 BCE/Toltec migration claim is internally anachronistic and is NOT used. Astronomical eclipse claim also omitted.

sources.title: INAH, Cempoala: la arquitectura del agua (2026)
sources.note: Full indexed original, 11 August 2026. Gravity-fed Actopan water, drainage, raised platforms and urban layout. Does not rely on the page’s unusually broad Late Postclassic date label.

sources.title: INPI, Totonacos: Etnografía
sources.note: Full relevant original indexed sections Historia, Organización social and Medicina tradicional verified. Modern ethnography explicitly identified; no universal timeless customs, supernatural efficacy, population-collapse percentage or total local animal extinction claims copied.

sources.title: INPI, Pueblo Tutunakuj o Totonaca
sources.note: Original indexed national catalogue establishes living community distribution, Papantla and Cuetzalan. Linguistic variant counts differ from INALI; no universal count copied.

sources.title: UNESCO, Totonac Centre for Indigenous Arts
sources.note: Official original indexed nomination summary read in full; direct page body challenge. House-schools, House of Elders, Totonac instruction, craft plants and reforestation.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ritual ceremony of the Voladores
sources.note: Official original indexed nomination summary verified; direct page body challenge. Four descending flyers plus caporal playing flute and drum; shared by several peoples, not solely Totonac.

sources.title: INALI, Totonaco/Tutunakuj courtesy phrases, by Elías García Aparicio
sources.note: Direct phrase list. Totonaco central del norte specifically. Tun Kuil’ / Buenos días; English Good morning translated from supplied Spanish. Modern Roman-letter writing, no ancient date implied.

sources.title: Mexico Secretariat of Culture, Atoles, tamales y fermentados de maíz del Totonacapan
sources.note: Original cultural-inventory account indexed; nixtamal, grinding on metate or in mill, comal tortillas and maize beverages. Living regional practice, not an exact 1492 recipe.

sources.title: Government of Veracruz, traditional cooks at Yolpaki (2026)
sources.note: Indexed original identifies Micaela Simbrón Rodríguez, Mujeres de Humo, Papantla, pulacles, bocoles and molotes. Later paragraph concerns a different Oaxacan cook and is not attributed to her.

sources.title: INAH, Zona Arqueológica de Cuicuilco
sources.note: Indexed original Relevancia cultural read. Strategic delta, resources and early/protourban identity. The page’s chronology line mixes conflicting endpoints and is not adopted.

sources.title: INAH, Cuicuilco archaeological site and individual structures
sources.note: Full relevant indexed original, including expanded Cuicuilco A details: eight enlargements 800 to 150 BCE, Kiva painting, E1 burial, tripod vessels. Its circa 250 CE eruption date is not adopted as settled.

sources.title: Felipe Ramírez and Alejandro Pastrana, Reinterpretando Cuicuilco
sources.note: Primary article, Arqueología 65, pages 4 to 33, uploaded 2024; also cited as 2021 in later paper. Direct fetch failed; original indexed PDF and indexed official PDF viewer provided text and Figure 20. Same article is one source regardless of URL variants. Exact claims bounded to irrigation, carved Estela and later activity.

sources.title: Georgina Ibarra-Arzave and colleagues, Biogeoarcheological evidence of soil management at Cuicuilco (2026)
sources.note: Original publisher article indexed in full relevant sections 2.2, 2.4, 3.1 and 5.2. Reused old soils, multiple analytic indicators and charred maize context. Direct fetch failed; no claim that ancient soil carbon directly dates a building.

sources.title: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Chichinautzin: Xitle eruption
sources.note: Direct institutional volcano entry. Eruption sequence and burial of Cuicuilco/agricultural land, not a single unqualified eruption year.

sources.title: Urrutia-Fucugauchi and colleagues, Archaeomagnetic dating of the Xitle eruption (2016)
sources.note: Direct primary article record and abstract; estimated circa 90 BCE to 20 CE. Presented as one study, contrasted with later calibration, not merged into a false consensus.

sources.title: Deciphering chemical complexity in monogenetic eruptions: Xitle Volcano, Mexico (2026)
sources.note: Original publisher indexed text explicitly places onset shortly after 380 to 400 CE, citing Siebe 2000 and recalibrations in Siebe et al. 2024. Used only for qualified contrasting chronology; direct fetch failed.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Partial Veracruz/Puebla outline, not a verified total Totonac territory or timeless state. Cempoala is a regional contextual example beyond the narrow polygon’s eastern edge. No Veracruz-civilization or distinct Classic cultural identity absorbed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Opening erroneous 900 BCE/Toltec-migration statement in the INAH site page intentionally excluded. 1200 contextual period is not an asserted foundation. Later community evidence explicitly labeled modern.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: INALI modern Tutunakuj central-northern variety Tun Kuil’ / Buenos días, English Good morning. Directly checked, not a pan-Totonac or preconquest spelling.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Geometry at the archaeological site in southern Mexico City, but imported 1492 to 1500 phase is anachronistic for the major Preclassic center. Public first paragraph explicitly warns not an independent fifteenth-century kingdom. Later scattered activity must not be equated with continued city-state sovereignty.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Institutional pages conflict internally and with published geochronology. Public chronology distinguishes 2016 archaeomagnetic circa 90 BCE to 20 CE from later 380 to 400 CE onset interpretation. No exact item years supplied. Root may later correct imported phase separately; narrative does not silently validate it.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Carved circles and diamonds are attested on the Estela; checked research does not provide a deciphered sentence. No invented language specimen or simplistic universal illiteracy claim.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No direct evidence of a particular toilet design, exact lifespan, or specific home remedy found and none invented. Daily-life evidence instead covers pots, water management, maize and construction labor.
